hints.title: Use the coefficient restrictions in standard form
hints.body: The three positive numbers are in standard form, so 1≤a,b,c<10. Multiplying the given equality by 1000 gives a+10b=100c.
hints.recap: Standard form supplies bounds on the leading coefficients as well as powers of ten.
hints.pitfall: A leading coefficient of 10 is not in standard form.
hints.pause: Use c≥1 and a<10 to bound b.

recall.reminder: Align powers of ten while keeping the standard-form restrictions.

hints.title: Use both endpoint bounds
hints.body: Start from 10b=100c−a: apply the lower bound on c and the strict upper bound on a. Then bound c using its expression in terms of a and b.
hints.recap: Strict coefficient bounds can force a strict conclusion.
hints.pitfall: The coefficients need not be integers.
hints.pause: Derive the b and c bounds and compare them.

recall.reminder: Strict coefficient bounds can force a strict conclusion.

hints.title: Test whether a is forced
hints.body: Try a coefficient a comfortably inside its allowed interval, then solve for b using a small admissible c near one. Check all standard-form bounds.
hints.recap: A must-be-true claim can be refuted by one admissible triple.
hints.pitfall: The triple must satisfy both the equation and every coefficient bound.
hints.pause: Build a valid example and test the remaining claims about a.

recall.reminder: A must-be-true claim can be refuted by one admissible triple.

solution:
1≤a,b,c<10 and a+10b=100c. Hence 10b=100c−a>90, so b>9 is forced. Meanwhile c<1.1, so b<c is impossible.

The allowed example a=8,b=9.3,c=1.01 has neither a>9 nor a<c. Therefore only II must be true. Answer B.
knowledgePattern: Use standard-form mantissa bounds to force a decimal carry
